sections.executive_summary:
### Opportunity snapshot
California serves adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities (I/DD) in small licensed homes. The home is licensed by CDSS Community Care Licensing as an **Adult Residential Facility (ARF)** and paid by one of 21 **regional centers** once it is vendored under Title 17 [S52][S25]. Payment is a **monthly rate per resident set by DDS**, so there is no rate to negotiate. The rate depends on the home's **service level**, its **size** (4 or fewer beds is paid more than 5+), whether it is **staff- or owner-operated**, and the **regional center's cost tier** [S2].

Rate reform changed the business in 2025:
- Since January 1, 2025 the old 11 levels (2, 3, 4A–4I) are paid as **Levels 2–6** plus a customizable **Level 7** [S6].
- Rates are split into a **90% base** and a **10% Quality Incentive Program (QIP)** amount that must be earned [S6][S7].
- The hold-harmless protection for vendors above the new rates ended at the end of February 2026 [S8].
- Current rates took effect **July 1, 2026** [S1][S2].

Demand is steady, not booming:
- DDS served **519,111 people in December 2025**; **32,940** lived in community care homes, **25,603** of them adults [S10][S11].
- Community-care-home residents rose only about 5% since December 2020, while the overall caseload grew about 42% [S10]. Most growth is people living at home with family.
- **152,976 adults live with a parent or guardian**, including 21,964 age 42+ [S11]. That is the future pipeline as parents age.

### The bottom line of the model
At the current base rates (San Diego/Orange/North LA tier) and 90% occupancy:
- **4-bed Level 6 (old 4I): +$2,695/month.** This is the configuration that works. Break-even occupancy is 84%.
- **Two 4-bed Level 6 homes sharing an administrator: +$5,223/month.**
- **6-bed Level 4: +$824/month** (thin).
- **4-bed Level 4: −$1,733/month; 4-bed Level 3: −$2,226/month.** These lose money unless the home stays nearly full or earns the QIP 10%.

These results staff each home at the hours DDS built into its rate models. The rent assumed is coastal-metro rent. Earning the QIP adds $4,438/month to a 4-bed Level 6 home (Section 8).

### Key numbers (verified)
See the table above. Every figure traces to the sources list.

### What this report does not claim
See the 'not claimed' list: no residential waitlist, no occupancy data, no current count of vendored homes by level, and no Level 7, ARFPSHN, EBSH or CCH rates.
sections.service_model:
### Who is served
Adults (18+) who are regional center clients under the Lanterman Act and need 24-hour care and supervision outside the family home [S9][S14]. Residents typically attend day programs or work during the day. The home supports daily living skills, health, behavior and community participation under each person's Individual Program Plan (IPP) [S16].

### Two layers of rules
| Layer | Agency | What it controls | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| License | CDSS Community Care Licensing | Health and safety, building, administrator certificate, personnel, records, inspections | HSC §1500 et seq.; 22 CCR §80000 (general) and §85000 (ARF) [S29][S30] |
| Vendorization + service level | Regional center (DDS rules) | Program design, service level, staffing hours, consultant hours, staff training, reports, payment | 17 CCR §54300 et seq. and §56001 et seq. [S22][S14] |

A home must hold the CCL license **and** be vendored before the regional center can place anyone or pay [S23][S24].

### Service codes
- **905** — residential facility serving adults, **owner-operated**: the home is the residence of the licensee or a corporate board member [S25].
- **915** — residential facility serving adults, **staff-operated**: not the licensee's residence; employees provide care [S25].
- 910 and 920 are the owner- and staff-operated codes for **children** (not adults) [S25].
- **113** is now used only for ARFs for Persons with Special Health Care Needs (ARFPSHN); former 'specialized residential facilities' moved to 905–920 in 2025 [S6].

### Service levels after rate reform
| Rate level (2025+) | Title 17 levels it replaces | Basic staffing rule (17 CCR §56004) | Consultant hours per resident per 6 months |
|---|---|---|---|
| Level 2 | 2 | 1 direct care staff per up to 6 | — |
| Level 3 | 3, 4A, 4B | 1 per up to 3 | 4A/4B: 8 |
| Level 4 | 4C, 4D, 4E | 1 per up to 2 | 8 (4C), 12 (4D–4E) |
| Level 5 | 4F, 4G, 4H | 1 for the first resident, plus added hours | 12 (4F), 16 (4G–4H) |
| Level 6 | 4I | 1 for the first resident, plus added hours | 16 |
| Level 7 | Above Level 6 | Customized | Customized |

Sources: crosswalk [S6]; staffing and consultant rules [S14]. Title 17 still uses the 4A–4I names; the regional center approves the level from your program design within 45 days [S15].

### Related models (not modeled here)
- **Enhanced Behavioral Supports Homes (EBSH)** and **Community Crisis Homes (CCH)** are ARFs certified by DDS under separate regulations; DDS lists their regulations on its regulations page [S55][S52].
- **ARFPSHN (113)** serves people with significant health needs and uses a customizable rate [S6].
- These carry negotiated or customized rates that are not published, so they are not modeled [S2].
sections.licensing_pathway:
### Step 1 — Form the business
- Form an LLC or corporation with the Secretary of State: LLC-1 $70; Statement of Information $20 [S64].
- California LLCs owe an **$800 annual tax** plus a gross-receipts LLC fee ($900 at $250k–$499,999; $2,500 at $500k–$999,999; $6,000 at $1M–$4.99M) [S63].

### Step 2 — Administrator certification
- An ARF must have a **certified administrator** who is at least 21 and has a high school diploma or GED [S31].
- Certification: complete the **35-hour Initial Certification Training Program**, pass the state exam within 60 days (3 attempts), then apply within 30 days on LIC 9214 with Live Scan [S32].
- Fees: exam **$100**; application **$140** [S34].
- Renewal: **40 hours of CE every two years** [S33]. Up to 24 hours of regional-center-approved DDS training can count toward the 40 [S33].
- Homes of 7–15 clients need an administrator with one year of residential care experience [S31].
- Title 17 adds DD experience for administrators: Level 2 = 6 months, Level 3 = 9 months, Level 4 = 12 months. The regional center can waive this [S17].

### Step 3 — CCL orientation and application
1. **Component I** online Adult orientation: $50 + $4.85 [S53]. The orientation is required before filing [S29].
2. Prepare the application:
   - LIC 281 application [S52]
   - plan of operation [S41]
   - **LIC 9282 infection control plan** (required for ARFs) [S52]
   - administrator certificate, fire authority information, Live Scan and health screenings [S52][S43][S42]
   - a **financial plan showing start-up funds for the first three months of operation** [S30]
3. Pay the **application fee with the application**: $908 for 4–6 beds ($454 for 1–3; $1,363 for 7–15) [S48].
4. **Component II** interview with the analyst, then a **pre-licensing inspection**, then **Component III** (operations and record keeping) before licensure [S53][S52].
5. CAB checks: criminal record, overconcentration, documents, start-up funds, credit and compliance history [S52]. Expect **90–120 days** for the whole process [S52].
6. The **annual fee** ($454 for 4–6 beds) is due each year; late payment adds 50% [S48].

### Location rules
- A home for **six or fewer** is a **residential use**: no conditional use permit or zoning variance [S49].
- It is exempt from local business taxes, registration fees and use-permit fees. Fire-inspection fees are barred except under HSC §13235 [S50].
- **Overconcentration:** CDSS can deny a license if residential facilities would be within **300 feet** of each other. RCFEs and foster family homes do not count [S51].
- **Fire clearance** is requested through CCL. A separate clearance is needed before admitting **nonambulatory** residents or anyone 65+ [S40].
- Bedrooms: no more than **two clients** per bedroom [S38].
- Bathrooms: one toilet and washbasin per 6 persons; one tub or shower per 10, counting staff and family who live there [S39].

### Step 4 — Regional center vendorization (in parallel)
1. Attend the regional center's **residential services orientation**. The administrator must complete it before the first admission [S20].
2. **Standardized vendorization** has run through the DDS **Provider Directory** since 1/1/2026 [S26][S27]:
   - Create a profile and submit minimum requirements. The regional center has **15 days** to decide.
   - Submit the full packet. The regional center has **30 days** to confirm it is complete; you have **30 days** to cure gaps.
   - The regional center **approves or denies within 45 days** and issues a vendor number.
3. The packet includes:
   - DS 1890 vendor application, disclosures and the signed HCBS Provider Agreement [S22]
   - a **program design** (17 CCR §56013): organizational chart, purpose, services and outcomes, entrance/exit criteria, program preparation duties, staff qualifications and duty statements, sample staff schedule, and training plan. Level 3 and Level 4 designs have extra content requirements [S16].
   - a written request for the **service level**, with the administrator's qualifications. The regional center decides within **45 days** [S15].
4. The regional center may process the vendor application up to approval while the license is pending, but it **cannot approve vendorization or refer anyone until the license is issued** [S23]. It cannot pay for services before vendorization [S24].

### Realistic overall timeline
About 4–8 months from LLC formation to first admission:
- 90–120 days for licensing [S52]
- vendor steps of up to 15 + 30 (+30 cure) + 45 days [S27], which can run in parallel
- property search and staff hiring (operator estimate — verify locally)
sections.reimbursement:
### How money flows
Each resident's monthly ARM rate has two parts [S1][S2]:
1. **SSI/SSP board-and-care amount — $1,444.07/month**, paid by the resident from SSI/SSP. The resident keeps **$182** for personal and incidental needs [S1][S68]. For context, the 2026 federal SSI benefit is $994 [S70].
2. **Regional center payment** = full rate − $1,444.07. The regional center pays from DDS purchase-of-service funds, with federal HCBS waiver match where the resident is eligible [S9].

The rate is **payment in full**. Vendors may not bill families a supplement for authorized services [S24].

### Base rate vs. Quality Incentive Program
- DDS rate files publish the **full rate** and a **base rate** = (full − $1,444.07) × 90% + $1,444.07 [S2].
- The remaining 10% is the **QIP** amount. Residential codes 905/915/113 are on the Quality Incentive Rate, and the residential measure is **Prevention & Wellness** (residents get preventive screenings on schedule) [S7].
- QIP eligibility requires HCBS settings compliance, EVV compliance where applicable, and independent audit/review compliance [S7]. The 2026-27 budget books a $333.9 million reduction for the QIP eligibility mandate [S8].
- **This model uses the base rate.** A new vendor should not count on the QIP until DDS confirms eligibility.

### 2026 residential rates (effective July 1, 2026, adults, staff-operated 915)
| Level | 4 or fewer beds — full | 4 or fewer — base (90%) | 5–6 beds — full |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 (old 2) | $6,789.37 | $6,254.84 | $5,422.47 |
| 3 (old 3, 4A, 4B) | $8,457.87 | $7,756.49 | $7,663.19 |
| 4 (old 4C–4E) | $9,892.30 | $9,047.48 | $9,218.29 |
| 5 (old 4F–4H) | $12,314.17 | $11,227.16 | $11,662.07 |
| 6 (old 4I) | $13,772.04 | $12,539.24 | $13,251.21 |

Notes on the table:
- Tier: SDRC, Harbor, Orange County, North LA, San Gabriel–Pomona and North Bay [S2]. 7+ beds pay the same as 5–6 [S2].
- Lower tier (Alta, Central Valley, Far Northern, Inland, Kern, Redwood Coast, Valley Mountain): Level 6 at 4 beds = $13,298.48 [S3].
- Highest tier: RCEB and San Andreas Level 6 = $15,350.62 [S4]; Golden Gate $15,309.57 [S71].
- Owner-operated (905) Level 2 and 3 rates are lower: Level 3 at 4 beds = $6,573.35. **New Level 4–6 homes get staff-operated rates whether or not the owner lives there** [S2][S6].
- **Supplemental Residential Program Support (109)** pays **$32.10/hour** (SDRC tier) when the regional center authorizes extra staff for an individual [S2].
- **Level 7** and **ARFPSHN (113)** rates are calculated by the regional center from staffing, consultant hours and fixed costs [S2][S6].

### What the rate model assumes you spend
DDS's rate models show what each rate is built to fund [S5]. For a **4-bed Level 4** home:
- 220 staff hours/week per facility, including 56 lead-staff hours and 21 administrator hours (one administrator shared by two homes)
- DSP wage $18.20, lead $19.58, administrator $25.24
- 24 consultant hours per resident per year at $123.50 (San Diego)
- food $270/person/month; 210 miles/week at $0.725/mile
- program operations $70/week per resident; 12% administration

Level 6 assumes **300 hours/week**; Level 3, **180** [S5]. Housing is funded through the SSI/SSP amount (about $5,776/month for four residents) [S5].

### Rate history and risk
Rate reform was phased in: partial increases came first, and full benchmark rates began January 1, 2025 [S6]. AB 2423 requires DDS to update and post the rate models every two years starting January 1, 2026. **Updates are paid only if the Legislature and the Administration fund them** [S1].
sections.demand:
### Who refers
Placements come from **regional center service coordinators** and residential/placement units, guided by each person's IPP. The regional center may not refer anyone to a home until it is vendored [S24]. There is no advertising-driven private-pay market.

### Size of the market (DDS data)
| Measure | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| People served by regional centers (all residence types), Dec 2025 | 519,111 | [S10] |
| Living in community care homes, Dec 2025 | 32,940 (25,603 age 18+) | [S10][S11] |
| Community care home residents, Dec 2020 | 31,413 | [S10] |
| Adults 18+ living with parent/guardian, Dec 2025 | 152,976 (21,964 age 42+; 9,269 age 52+) | [S11] |
| DDS community caseload forecast | 487,114 (FY 2025-26) → 526,848 (FY 2026-27) | [S9] |
| Residential Services purchase of services, FY 2026-27 | $7.41 billion | [S9] |

### Where the residents are (community care homes, Dec 2025) [S10]
Inland 4,250; San Diego 2,677; North LA 2,445; East Bay 2,251; Orange County 2,062; Alta California 2,058; Central Valley 2,009; South Central LA 1,873; San Andreas 1,666; Valley Mountain 1,588; San Gabriel–Pomona 1,555; Harbor 1,206; Golden Gate 1,163; North Bay 1,024; Tri-Counties 968; Far Northern 934; Kern 868; Eastern LA 754; Lanterman 702; Westside 659; Redwood Coast 228.

### What the data suggest
- **Slow, steady growth in residential placements.** Community-care-home residents grew about 5% (Dec 2020 → Dec 2025), while total people served grew about 42% [S10]. New homes compete mostly for turnover and for people leaving family homes.
- **Aging caregivers.** Nearly 22,000 adults age 42+ still live with a parent or guardian [S11]. Many will need out-of-home placement as parents age.
- **Older residents.** 6,129 community-care-home residents are 62+ [S11]. Health needs and end-of-life planning are rising.
- **Higher-acuity demand.** In the last published count by level (FY 2017-18), Level 4I was the largest and fastest-growing level (1,192 of 4,294 ARM homes, +7.8% that year), while Levels 2 and 3 shrank [S13]. This is old data; use it as direction only.

### How to confirm demand locally
Ask your regional center's community services/resource development unit:
- which levels, genders, ages and behavioral or medical profiles they need placements for
- whether they are funding any new homes through community placement plans (not verified here)

Get this in writing before you sign a lease.
sections.operations:
### Staffing rules that drive cost
- **Title 17 basic staffing** (whenever residents are under facility supervision) [S14]:
  - Level 2: 1 direct care staff per up to 6 residents
  - Levels 3/4A/4B: 1 per up to 3
  - 4C–4E: 1 per up to 2
  - 4F–4I: 1 for the first resident
  - Homes above these resident counts must add weekly direct care hours by level (a table in §56004(d)). Up to 2–7 hours per resident per week of program preparation can count toward them [S14].
- **Title 22:** staff in numbers needed to meet client needs; CCL can require more [S35][S42].
  - Day ratio for clients who rely on others for all ADLs: as the regional center specifies, never worse than **1:3** [S36].
  - Night (10 p.m.–7 a.m.): homes of 15 or fewer need one person **on call on the premises**. For regional center clients who rely on others for all ADLs, night staffing is **as the regional center requires** [S37].
  - Level 3+ homes in the DDS rate models are staffed **awake around the clock** (no overnight offset), and so is this P&L [S5].
- **Consultant hours** at Level 4: 8–16 per resident per six months, by level [S14].
- **Specialized skills** (for example nursing tasks) must be done by licensed or certified personnel [S35]. Unlicensed staff may assist with **self-administered** medications but may not give injections [S45].

### Modeled staffing (from the DDS rate models) [S5]
| Configuration | Facility hrs/week | Line | Lead | Administrator |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4-bed Level 3 | 180 | 103 | 56 | 21 |
| 4-bed Level 4 | 220 | 143 | 56 | 21 |
| 4-bed Level 6 | 300 | 223 | 56 | 21 |
| 6-bed Level 4 | 298.4 | 221.4 | 56 | 21 |
| Two 4-bed Level 6 | 600 | 446 | 112 | 42 |

Line and lead hours are multiplied by a **1.045 paid-hours factor**. It covers paid sick leave (40 hrs/yr) [S65] and paid time for required training [S19][S18]. It is an operator estimate; DDS's own models use 1.15 (Section 8).

### Training
| Who | Requirement | Source |
|---|---|---|
| New direct care staff | On-site orientation within the first 40 hours: program design, IPPs, rights, medications, emergencies, SIRs, abuse reporting | [S18] |
| Direct care staff | **DSPT**: two 35-hour competency-based segments (year 1 and year 2) with tests or a challenge test; free to DSPs | [S19][S28] |
| Direct care staff CE | 8 hrs/yr (L2), 12 hrs/yr (L3, L4); L4 staff without 6 months' experience add 12 hrs in the first 6 months | [S18] |
| Night staff | Emergency procedures and first aid | [S37] |
| Administrator | 35-hr ICTP + exam; 40 hrs CE / 2 yrs; Title 17 CE 8–12 hrs/yr (can overlap); HIV/TB training within 6 months | [S34][S33][S17][S31] |

### Required records and reporting
- **Needs and Services Plan before admission** [S47]. Plan of operation kept current [S41]. Personal rights posted and honored [S46].
- **Consumer notes** (activities, illness, medical visits, SIRs). Progress reports: **semiannual** at Levels 2–3; **quarterly** at Level 4, sent to the service coordinator within 30 days of quarter end [S21].
- **CCL incident reports** by the next working day, written report within 7 days [S44].
- **Special Incident Reports** to the regional center under Title 17. DDS's revised SIR regulations took effect **5/1/2026** [S55].
- **Mandated reporting** of dependent adult abuse [S69].
- **Vendor records** kept at least 5 years [S24].
- **Independent review** if regional center payments reach $500,000–$1,999,999 a year; **independent audit** at $2 million+. Reports are due 9 months after fiscal year end [S54].

### Labor law
- California minimum wage is **$16.90** (2026) [S56]. Local rates are higher, e.g. San Diego $17.75, San Jose $18.45 [S59], and from July 1, 2026: City of Los Angeles $18.42, unincorporated Los Angeles County $18.47, Pasadena $18.57, Milpitas $18.50, San Francisco and Berkeley $19.61, Emeryville $20.34 [S58].
- The DDS model's $18.20 DSP wage is **below those local minimums**, including unincorporated LA County and Pasadena, which sit in the SDRC-tier regional centers this model uses; those operators must pay more (Section 8).
- 24-hour shifts, sleep time and meal/rest rules for residential care need employment counsel (Wage Order 5; not separately verified here).
sections.market_conditions:
### Supply
- **6,128 licensed Adult Residential Facilities** with **40,041 beds** (May 2025) [S12]:
  - 2,818 are licensed for exactly 4 beds
  - 2,661 for 5–6 beds, 259 for 1–3, 175 for 7–15 and 215 for 16+
  - 401 more applications were pending
- Specialized types listed separately: 97 ARFPSHN homes (463 beds), 82 EBSH homes (309 beds), 25 Community Crisis Homes (103 beds) [S12].
- ARFs also serve non-DD adults (e.g., mental health), so these counts are not all regional center homes.
- **Churn:** the CCL list shows 512 new ARF licenses first issued in 2024 and 360 ARF closures in 2024 [S12].
- **Where:** most licensed ARFs are in Los Angeles (1,596), San Diego (577), Riverside (460), Orange (384), San Bernardino (380) and Sacramento (354) counties [S12].

### Why small homes dominate
4-bed homes are paid materially more per resident than 5–6-bed homes. At Level 6 the difference is $520.83 a month (full rate), but staffing does not scale down proportionally [S2][S5]. That explains the 2,818 four-bed licenses [S12].

### Wages (BLS OEWS May 2025, California) [S57][S72][S73]
| Role (SOC) | Statistic | Hourly |
|---|---|---|
| Home health & personal care aides (31-1120) | mean | $17.51 |
| Social & human service assistants (21-1093) | 25th pct / median | $22.17 / $24.56 |
| Social & community service managers (11-9151) | 25th pct / median | $34.04 / $40.01 |
| Registered nurses (29-1141) | mean | $72.25 |
| LVNs (29-2061) | mean | $39.59 |

The DDS rate models fund $18.20 for DSPs, $19.58 for lead staff and $25.24 for administrators at Levels 2–4 [S5]. **The P&L pays the administrator the BLS 11-9151 25th percentile ($34.04)**, which is above the rate-model figure, to stay conservative.

### Housing cost proxy (HUD FY2026 4-bedroom FMR) [S66]
- Sacramento $3,460; Riverside–San Bernardino $3,514; Los Angeles $3,672; San Diego $4,845; Orange County $5,246.
- The P&L uses $5,000 for a 4-bedroom home and $6,000 for a 5-bedroom home (operator estimates — verify locally).

### Trends to watch
- DDS caseload growth (+8% forecast for FY 2026-27) [S9].
- QIP eligibility enforcement and HCBS settings compliance [S7][S8].
- Rate-model updates every two years that need legislative funding [S1].
- Rising local minimum wages [S58][S59].
- Workers' comp: the average advisory benchmark is $1.65 per $100 of payroll from 9/1/2026 [S62].
sections.financial_narrative:
### How the pro forma is built
**Revenue per occupied bed** = the regional center's **base (90%)** payment + the **$1,444.07 SSI/SSP** amount from the resident [S2][S1]. All rates are the July 1, 2026 SDRC/Harbor/Orange/North LA tier:
- 4-bed Level 3 = $7,756.49
- 4-bed Level 4 = $9,047.48
- 4-bed Level 6 = $12,539.24
- 6-bed Level 4 = $8,440.87

**Staffing** follows the facility hours in the DDS rate models (table in Section 6) [S5]:
- DSP $18.20 and lead $19.58, the DDS model wages
- administrator $34.04 for 21 hrs/week per home (BLS 11-9151 25th percentile, May 2025) [S57][S73]
- payroll burden 17%: taxes about 9% [S60][S61], workers' comp 5% (operator estimate) [S62], other benefits 3%
- consultant hours at the DDS model's $123.50/hour [S5][S14]
- food at the USDA moderate plan, $367.10 (August 2026) [S67]
- mileage per the DDS model [S5]

**Fixed costs** include rent, utilities, insurance, the CDSS annual fee [S48], the LLC tax and fee sized to revenue [S63], and accounting. The two-home configuration adds an independent review [S54].

### Results at 90% occupancy (stabilized month)
| Configuration | Revenue | Expenses | Net | Break-even occupancy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4-bed Level 6 (default) | $45,141 | $42,447 | +$2,695 | 84% |
| Two 4-bed Level 6 | $90,283 | $85,060 | +$5,223 | 84% |
| 6-bed Level 4 | $45,581 | $44,757 | +$824 | 88% |
| 4-bed Level 4 | $32,571 | $34,304 | −$1,733 | 95% |
| 4-bed Level 3 | $27,923 | $30,149 | −$2,226 | 98% |

At **80% occupancy** every configuration loses money: 4-bed Level 6 −$1,972; two homes −$4,111. In a 4-bed home, one long vacancy is the difference between profit and loss.

### Sensitivity (4-bed Level 6, default +$2,695)
| Change | Effect | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Earn the QIP 10% (full rate) | +$4,438 | +$7,133 |
| QIP earned, less the independent review it triggers (~$500/month, operator estimate) [S54] | +$3,938 | +$6,633 |
| Pay City of Los Angeles minimum ($18.42) to line staff | −$260 | +$2,435 |
| Pay unincorporated LA County minimum ($18.47) to line staff (SDRC-tier catchments) | −$319 | +$2,376 |
| Pay San Francisco/Berkeley minimum ($19.61) to line and lead staff, same rate tier | −$1,675 | +$1,020 |
| Pay BLS 21-1093 25th percentile ($22.17) to line and lead staff [S72] | −$5,459 | −$2,764 |
| Use DDS's 1.15 paid-hours factor (PTO + supervision + training) instead of 1.045 | −$2,744 | −$50 |
| Lower rate tier (Central Valley/Inland etc., base $12,113.04), same rent | −$1,534 | +$1,161 |
| Highest tier (East Bay/San Andreas, base $13,959.97), same rent and wages | +$5,115 | +$7,810 |
| Each $1,000/month of rent | −$1,000 | |

- **4-bed Level 4** turns positive only with the QIP (+$1,308) or occupancy above 95%.
- At DDS's own 1.15 paid-hours factor every configuration loses money at 90% occupancy (two homes −$266; 6-bed Level 4 −$1,905; 4-bed Level 4 −$3,703; 4-bed Level 3 −$3,808). The 1.045 factor used here is an operator estimate; budget for real PTO, supervision and training time.
- At about 94%+ occupancy (the 97% optimistic case) or with the QIP, a single 4-bed Level 6 home's regional center payments exceed $500,000/yr and require a WIC §4652.5 independent review (~$6,000/yr, operator estimate — verify with a CPA) [S54]. The optimistic result in the P&L does not include it.
- Inland regions pay less, but HUD rents there are about $1,300–$1,400 lower than the $5,000 modeled [S66]. A lower-tier Level 6 home with inland rent is roughly as profitable as the default.

### Ramp-up and cash
The ramp assumes one admission a month (two homes: two a month). Real fill speed depends on regional center referrals. CAB requires proof of **three months of operating funds** before licensing [S30]: about $127,341 for a 4-bed Level 6 home. The workbook's modeled ramp-up deficit replaces that line in total cash needed.
sections.risks:
1. **Single payer, fixed rates.** One regional center decides placements and the level; DDS sets the rate [S2][S15]. Rate-model updates need legislative funding [S1].
2. **QIP uncertainty.** 10% of the regional center portion depends on QIP eligibility and measures. This is worth $4,438/month to a 4-bed Level 6 home [S7][S8].
3. **Vacancy.** One empty bed in a 4-bed home is 25% vacancy. The default home breaks even at 84% occupancy and loses $1,972/month at 80%.
4. **Level mismatch.** If residents' needs fall, or the regional center approves a lower level, revenue drops by roughly $1,300–$3,500 per resident per month (Level 6 → 4 base: $3,491.76) [S2][S15]. A level change is considered only on a change of ownership or when most residents' ID teams identify a new need [S15].
5. **Wages.** The modeled $18.20 is below several July 1, 2026 local minimums [S58]: City of Los Angeles $18.42, unincorporated Los Angeles County $18.47 and Pasadena $18.57 (both in SDRC-tier regional center areas), San Jose $18.45 [S59], San Francisco and Berkeley $19.61, and Emeryville $20.34. At $18.47 the default home nets +$2,376; at $19.61 for line and lead staff, +$1,020 (before the higher RCEB/GGRC tier rates those Bay Area homes receive). Paying the BLS 21-1093 25th percentile ($22.17) [S72] turns the default home to −$2,764. Using DDS's own 1.15 paid-hours factor instead of the 1.045 operator estimate puts the default home at break-even (−$50/month). California daily overtime is not modeled; staff schedules should avoid it.
6. **Behavioral risk.** Level 5–6 residents bring property damage, staff injury (workers' comp) and incident reporting [S44][S55]. Insurance and repair costs are operator estimates.
7. **Licensing delays.** 90–120 days at CCL [S52] plus vendorization; rent runs before revenue.
8. **Compliance.** Annual CCL inspections, regional center monitoring, SIRs, quarterly reports at Level 4, and independent review once regional center payments reach $500,000 a year [S21][S54]. A single 4-bed Level 6 home crosses that line at about 94% occupancy or once it earns the QIP (≈$515,000–$517,000/yr); budget about $6,000/yr for the review (operator estimate — verify with a CPA). Revocation risk if there is no certified administrator [S31].
9. **Overconcentration and fire clearance** can block a chosen house [S51][S40].
10. **Policy change.** HCBS settings compliance and QIP eligibility rules are tightening [S7][S8].
sections.recommendations:
1. **Design for Level 6 (old 4I) in a 4-bed home** if you have the clinical capability. It is the only single-home configuration that is clearly profitable at the base rate (+$2,695/month at 90%; break-even at 84% occupancy, and about −$50/month if paid hours run at DDS's 1.15 factor) [S2][S5]. Level 3–4 homes need the QIP or near-full occupancy.
2. **Talk to the regional center first.** Confirm the level, population and location they need, in writing, before signing a lease. Ask about community placement plan funding (not verified here).
3. **Stay at 4 beds.** The 4-or-fewer rate premium beats the extra bed at Levels 3–6 [S2].
4. **Plan for two homes under one administrator.** That is DDS's own model assumption [S5]. Two Level 6 homes net +$5,223/month at 90% in this model.
5. **Qualify for the QIP from day one.** Complete the Provider Directory profile; meet HCBS settings, EVV (if applicable) and audit/review requirements; track residents' preventive screenings for the Prevention & Wellness measure [S7]. The QIP adds $4,438/month at Level 6.
6. **Get the administrator experience right.** Level 4 needs 12 months of DD experience (waivable) and an ARF certificate [S17][S34]. The licensee can be the administrator.
7. **Budget cash for six months, not three.** CAB verifies three months of operating funds [S30]; the ramp and referral timing usually take longer.
8. **Hire to the DDS hours, pay above local minimum, and enroll every DSP in DSPT** within year 1 and year 2 [S19][S28].
9. **Pick the house for licensing:** at least 300 ft from other residential facilities [S51]; bedrooms for two at most [S38]; bathrooms per §85088 [S39]; single-story or accessible if you will accept nonambulatory residents (separate fire clearance) [S40].
10. **Reprice the P&L for your regional center's tier and your city's wage floor** before committing [S3][S4][S58].

corrections_vs_previous: Old CVRC report described the rate structure as Levels 1–4 with sub-levels 4A–4I. Since January 1, 2025 regional centers pay Levels 2–6 plus customizable Level 7 (L3 = old 3/4A/4B, L4 = 4C–4E, L5 = 4F–4H, L6 = 4I) (DDS Residential directive).

Old report's rate table (e.g., $9,428.87 Level 4 and $13,066.98 Level 6, 4 beds, CVRC) is out of date and was presented as what the provider is paid. July 1, 2026 CVRC-tier rates are $9,591.58 and $13,298.48 full, and a new vendor is paid the 90% base ($8,776.83 and $12,113.04) unless it earns the QIP 10% (DDS Rates Effective Jul 2026).
Old report put the SSI room-and-board portion at about $1,420 and the personal allowance at about $177. For 2026 they are $1,444.07 and $182.00 (DDS rate page; ACWDL 25-29).

Old report cited California minimum wage as $15.50 (2023) and DSP pay of $16–$18 without a source. The 2026 state minimum is $16.90 (higher in many cities); the DDS rate models fund $18.20 for DSPs and $19.58 for lead staff.

Old P&L modeled 6 residents at a single Level 4I rate of $12,015.70 each, with no SSI/regional-center split, full rate from month 4, and #VALUE! errors in COGS. Current 5–6-bed Level 6 rates are $12,789.26–$14,764.95 full depending on tier ($11,654.74 base in the CVRC tier), and 4-bed homes earn more per resident.

Old report said 'issue a provisional license, followed by a regular license' and gave no CCL fee or timeline. CAB gives 90–120 days; the application fee for 4–6 beds is $908 with a $454 annual fee (HSC §1523.1).

Old report did not cover the standardized vendorization process (Provider Directory; 15/30/45-day steps since 1/1/2026), the 45-day service level decision (17 CCR §56005), or the start-up funds rule (22 CCR §85018).
Task framing listed service codes 910/915 for adults; per 17 CCR §54342, adult homes are 905 (owner-operated) and 915 (staff-operated); 910 and 920 are children's homes.
